ut_oquirrh_mountains.blurb: Utah's West Desert holds the Oquirrh range, which runs north to south on the west side of the Salt Lake Valley. The climbing splits fairly evenly between sport routes and boulder problems. Sport lines run from 5.8 to 5.12, with most at 5.10 and 5.11. Boulder problems range from the easiest grades up to V9, with plenty of V0 to V3 and a handful of hard ones. Ophir Canyon holds the most climbs, and limestone makes up most of its rock. Lake Point Crag, Zion's Crag and Blackridge Boulders add more, the last two leaning toward bouldering. Across the West Desert, most climbing is best in spring and fall, though high elevation spots in the Oquirrh range are pleasant in summer.

vt_bolton_notch_rd_boulders.blurb: These boulders lie within hiking distance of the Bolton Notch road, in the Bolton area of northern Vermont, about half an hour from downtown Burlington. Every climb is a boulder problem, spread from V0 up into double digits, with a healthy number of moderates around V1 to V4 and a solid hard end, including a cluster at V7 and another at V10. Kook Boulder holds the most climbs, followed by Ship's Prow and Alien Boulder, while the Halloween Boulder area and Tunnel Boulder Area are the other larger clusters. Across the wider Bolton area the rock is green schist, ranging from very sound to fairly loose.

wv_needleseye_boulder_park.blurb: Needleseye Boulder Park is in Oak Hill, West Virginia, near the New River Gorge. Large boulders and a cliff line stretching over two miles sit among forest, with sandstone cliffs reaching up to 80 feet. Many of the boulders and lower cliffs are short enough to climb without a harness or rope. Bouldering dominates, mostly V0 to V4 with a tail of harder problems up to V10. A smaller roped section adds sport routes and a few trad lines, from about 5.9 to 5.12. East Side Boulders, Entrance Boulders and Central Area Boulders hold the most boulder problems, and Needleseye Roped Climbing is the section for rope work.

ab_the_back_of_the_lake.blurb: Back of the Lake is a series of cliffs at the western edge of Lake Louise in the Bow Valley, in Banff National Park at about 5,000 feet. The rock is solid quartzite, and the climbing is generally vertical to gently overhanging, with a lot of steep ground. Sport routes outnumber trad. Most lines fall between 5.10 and 5.12, with a modest number of moderates below that and a few at 5.13. Outhouse Wall holds the most climbs, and Air Voyage and Amphitheater add more, mostly trad. Many routes can be climbed in summer, even in light rain.

az_pusch_ridge.blurb: Pusch Ridge is on the northwest side of the Santa Catalina Mountains, north of Tucson. The range is built of granite and gneiss. Trad leads the roped climbing here, mostly 5.9 and 5.10 with some easier routes and a few at 5.11 and 5.12, and boulder problems fill much of the rest across a wide spread of grades. Linda Vista holds the most climbs and offers moderate roped climbing and bouldering with a short approach. The Ozzy Cliff Bands is backcountry desert trad, with routes from 5.5 to 5.12 that mostly face northwest, shaded in the morning and sunny from about 1 to 5 pm in high season. Reaching it takes a hike of about three miles up Pima Canyon.
